name: RBUC Residual Coding
definition: Variable-length lossless coding for residuals. Based on RBUC, which amortizes length bits over several consecutive residuals using a tree structure. Each interior node stores w = max_i(ceil(log2(x_i + 1))) over child nodes with unsigned values x_i. Residuals are mapped to unsigned ordinals (0, -1, +1, -2, +2...) for computing w. Trees are shallow (4 levels for residuals up to 127 bits). Static branching is used: lowest-level branching factor 4-5 vertices, second-level branching ~16 nodes. Trees avoid grouping residuals from end of one row with start of next (spatial locality). Each row partitioned into groups of 3-5 vertices, second-level groups span whole rows.
